validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE FLAG. The gem.wiki page (read for leads only, not cited) carries NO location, NO named endpoints, NO start year, and exactly ONE citation: 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75'. I fetched that OPEC ASB 2012 PDF and ran url_verifier: it returns HTTP 200 but does NOT contain the token 'Najaf' (FAIL missing expected). OPEC's ASB reports only AGGREGATE downstream/pipeline statistics per member country, not individually named pipelines, so the sole cited source does not name this pipeline or corroborate any of its attributes (37 km / 16 in / 2.1 bcm/y). Per the sweep rule, a row whose only support is a generic/aggregate citation that does not name the pipeline is itself an existence flag. Independent searching (EN + AR: Iraqi press, oil-ministry, power-station and gas-company terms) surfaced only (a) the Najaf thermal power station, (b) the State Company for Gas Filling & Services / Najaf branch (LPG bottling, not a transmission line), and (c) generic national-gas-network history (rawabetcenter.com), which confirms Iraq's grid reaches Najaf and Hilla as consumption centers but names NO discrete 'Strategic-Najaf' line and gives none of its specs. So a gas lateral serving Najaf is physically PLAUSIBLE, but this specific named 37 km / 16-in / 2.1 bcm/y operating entity is unverified by any independent, pipeline-naming source. DUPLICATE RISK: this 'Strategic-*' Najaf/Hilla/Kabesa cluster (P1846/P1847/P1848, all last-edited 2023-09-09) overlaps in purpose with the 2022-vintage 'Trans-Iraqi-*' cluster, notably P4064 Trans-Iraqi-Najaf PWR St Gas Pipeline (74 km, 24 in) which also feeds Najaf; the two may be duplicate representations of one Najaf gas-supply corridor drawn from different source tables. Specs differ (37/16 vs 74/24), so I flag rather than assert the duplicate. CLASSIFICATION: named as gas and consistent with a dry-gas supply lateral to the Najaf power complex; no evidence it is one of the GulfPub crude/NGL lines (none of which touch Najaf), so classification is probably fine conditional on existence. ATTRIBUTION: Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' is generic-plausible but likewise uncited/unverified. Bottom line: cannot confirm existence on independent evidence; the whole row rests on an aggregate OPEC citation that does not mention Najaf.

routes.corridor_desc: Corridor is only loosely bounded. Independent national-gas-network history (rawabetcenter.com) confirms Iraq's grid extends from the south up through the center to Baghdad and lists Najaf and Hilla among the fed consumption centers, so a Najaf gas lateral would tap that central Euphrates trunk and run ~37 km into Najaf governorate, terminating at the Najaf power/industrial demand cluster (Najaf city ~32.0N 44.34E; Bahr al-Najaf power station lies ~15-20 km SW of the city). The upstream tap point is NOT independently sourced: a 37 km radius from Najaf would place it somewhere around the Kufa / Abu Sukhayr / Diwaniyah-direction trunk, but I will not fabricate a coordinate for it. Only the Najaf-end demand center is defensible from a named place; treat the origin as unknown.
routes.researcher_notes: End coordinate (Najaf city, ~32.0N 44.34E) is a well-established real place, used as the demand-center terminus; exact delivery facility (power station vs city gate) is not sourced. Start/tap coordinate left null deliberately — no independent source gives the upstream origin, and per standing rules I did not invent one. Corridor bound is wide (low accuracy). No route-repo edits made; this is a suggestion only.
